Dispatch charter is essentially written by AGENTS.md already: hoist the dynamic `import()` into the test file's module scope; ⛔ do NOT raise the timeout, ⛔ do NOT add the file to `heavyDomTests`, ⛔ do NOT weaken the anti-inert assertion (the card is explicit that this is THE one non-vacuous case in the file). Open diagnostic for the dev: whether the unbounded import is `FormPage`'s own `React.lazy` or one reached through `@object-ui/react`'s registry — capture the failure dump under load if needed. **Dispatch — `domain:ui` execution seat @ objectui, round 32. Bug tier.**

Claim: session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, branch `claude/issue-6567-formpage-predicatescope-flake`. Assigned by the PM.

## 1. This is a Bug with a named root cause, not a flake to retry

⛔ **"Flaky" is not a root cause and is not a licence to re-run.** The card names the mechanism: an **unbounded module load counted inside a bounded window**, which is the shape AGENTS.md §测试纪律 declares against. That makes this declared-≠-enforced on the test itself, which is why triage graded it Bug.

Triage's charter, binding:

> hoist the dynamic `import()` into the test file's module scope; ⛔ do NOT raise the timeout, ⛔ do NOT add the file to `heavyDomTests`, ⛔ do NOT weaken the anti-inert assertion (the card is explicit that this is THE one non-vacuous case in the file).

All three prohibitions are gate weakening in different clothes. Raising the timeout hides the unbounded load; `heavyDomTests` moves it to a lane where the same load is merely tolerated; weakening the assertion removes the reason the file exists.

## 2. Census — verify independently, your reading wins

- **File:** `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx`.
- **Exactly one dynamic import**, and it is the target: `:344` — `const { InternalFormRoute } = await import('./InternalFormRoute');`, inside the test body. That is the unbounded load sitting in the bounded window.
- **The anti-inert case is `:336`**, and the file says so itself at `:337`: *"⚠️ THE anti-inert case. Every other DENIED case above hands `FormPage` a …"*. `:29` and `:146` explain it is the case that would have caught a hop-2-only regression.
- **`heavyDomTests` is real** (`vitest.config.mts:92`) and this file is **not** in it. Keep it that way.

So the fix is one hoist, one site.

⭐ Note what the anti-inert case being the flaky one means, because it is the whole reason this is worth a Bug: a red there does not merely fail a test — it pressures **the single assertion that makes the other seven non-vacuous**. A quarantine or a timeout bump would leave seven cases that pass whether or not the code works.

## 3. The open diagnostic

Triage left one question for you, and it is worth answering rather than routing around: **is the unbounded import `FormPage`'s own `React.lazy`, or one reached through `@object-ui/react`'s registry?** Capture the failure dump under load if you need it. The hoist may well fix the symptom either way — say which cause you established, and if you could not establish it, say that instead of implying you did.

## 4. Verification

A flake fix is the easiest kind to prove wrongly, because "it passed" is what you saw before the fix too, most of the time. So:

- **Reproduce the failure first.** The card carries a repro table with three bracketing runs; the filer measured green in isolation and green in 2 of 3 full runs. A fix you cannot see failing beforehand is a fix you cannot show working.
- Then show the same full-project run passing, and say how many runs you did. One green run after an intermittent failure is not evidence.
- **Confirm the hoist did not change what the test exercises** — same module, same binding, still loaded before the timed window rather than during it.

## 5. Scope

`apps/console/src/components/FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx` and a changeset if the gates say one is owed — ask `check-changeset-presence` rather than assuming, in either direction. ⛔ No `vitest.config.mts`. ⛔ No timeout constants. ⛔ No assertion changes.

Shadow check: no in-flight card touches `apps/console/src/components/`. #6357 is in `packages/`, #6557 in `packages/app-shell/src/views/` and `packages/react/src/hooks/`.

⭐ Provenance: this card came from the #3719 dev, who hit the flake, established it was unrelated to its own diff (no import path from `pages/settings/`), searched 254 open issues before filing, and did **not** fold it in. That is why it is a clean card rather than a rider.

**Note for the PM on the changeset:** asked rather than assumed, in both directions. `check-changeset-presence` said one **is** owed (`apps/console` is a released package) and named the empty-frontmatter form as the pass for a change that publishes nothing — that is what the PR carries. No `skip-changeset` label was created or applied: that label does not exist in this repo, and applying one would silently mint a repository label for the next agent to misread.

**One thing worth carrying forward beyond this card.** The cost here was not `InternalFormRoute` — it was `@object-ui/app-shell` resolving to source through a `vi.mock(..., importOriginal)` factory, triggered by whatever first requests it as a *value*. Any console test whose first app-shell value request happens inside a test body has the same 10s bomb, and `apps/console` is the project that pays this because its vitest config alone points `@object-ui/app-shell` at `packages/app-shell/src`. I did not sweep for other instances — that would have been scope creep on a Bug-tier card — and I am not filing it as a finding on my own judgement, because a census is needed before anyone can say whether there are zero others or twenty. Flagging it for triage to decide whether that census is worth a card.

**Post-merge verification — PR #6579 merged 2026-08-26T14:43Z. Measured on `main`, all axes clean.**

**The fix.** `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx` is 397 lines. `await import('./InternalFormRoute')` occurs **0** times; the module-scope form is present at `:91`. The `vi.mock` hoisting note this PR added is at `:342`.

**The three shortcuts, each checked on `main` rather than on the diff.** These are the ways a failing test can be made to stop failing without being fixed, and the point of checking after the merge is that none of them crept back in:

| shortcut | measured | control |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| raise the timeout | **0** timeout-shaped lines in the file | the file *does* contain **12** four-digit-or-longer numbers, so the pattern reaches real content |
| add the file to `heavyDomTests` | **0** entries mentioning `predicateScope` or `FormPage` | `heavyDomTests` parses to **30** entries, so the list was actually read |
| skip / quarantine | **0** `.skip` / `.only`; **8** cases still declared; the anti-inert case is still there at `:366` with its `⚠️ THE anti-inert case.` marker | — |

Worth naming what those twelve numbers are, since a bare "0 timeout literals" against a file that plainly contains `15000` would be a suspicious claim: they are issue numbers (`6110`, `6010`, `4109`, ADR-`0068`), a copyright year, and the **prose** recording the measurement — *"it cost **10204ms** of `hop1SessionPrincipal`'s 15000ms budget"*. That `15000` describes the existing budget; it does not set one.

## Correction — this verification's first pass used two broken instruments

Both failed silently in the direction that would have produced a false all-clear, and both were caught by their own controls rather than by suspicion:

- The `heavyDomTests` check reported `predicateScope: 0` **and** `entries total: 0`. A list with zero entries cannot contain anything, so the reassuring number was meaningless; a shell-quoting error had stopped the pattern reaching the file. Re-run properly, the list has 30 entries and the answer is the same — but now it is measured.
- The timeout check printed nothing at all, neither a hit nor its "none found" fallback, because the `||` in `grep … | sed … || echo` binds to `sed`, which succeeds on empty input. The absence of output looked like a clean result and was actually no result.

Recording it because the lesson is the reusable part: **a zero is not a finding until a positive control fires in the same query, on the same data.** Twice in one command here, the control was the only thing standing between a broken instrument and a "verified clean" that had verified nothing.

Nothing outstanding on this card.
